panel.title: Kraftvakt
panel.not_loaded: Kraftvakt is not loaded. Check the integration under Settings → Devices & services.

status.stopped_info: The regulation is stopped, and all regulated appliances and EV chargers are turned off. The configuration can be changed. When the regulation starts, the appliances are turned on again one by one.
status.start_refused: The regulation cannot start before the configuration is complete.
status.safe_state_text: The power sensor {sensor} gives no valid measurement. All regulated appliances and EV chargers are turned off. The regulation starts again by itself when the sensor gives a valid value again.
status.penalty_text: The tariff average has been above the power limit. All regulated appliances and EV chargers are kept off until the overconsumption is recovered.
status.safe_state_back_text: The power sensor {sensor} gives a valid value again. The regulation starts again with everything off at the next decision.
status.no_chargers: No EV chargers in the group.
status.waiting_ends_at: Turns on at the decision at {time}
status.power_to_free_turn_on: {power} kW must be freed before it is turned on
status.power_to_free_activate: {power} kW must be freed before the EV charger is activated
status.power_to_free_ampere: {power} kW must be freed before the EV charger gets one more ampere
status.waiting_charger: Queued: another EV charger in the group has its turn
status.starting_until: Waiting until {time} for the car to start charging. Its power at minimum current is kept free until then.
status.activated_not_charging: Activated: the car does not draw power, so it waits at the minimum current
status.finishing_at: Finishing the charging that went on when the charging window ended, at {current} A
status.fault: A fault flag shows a fault, so the EV charger is deactivated until the fault clears
status.power_runs_out: The power runs out here. What is below waits for free power.
status.queued_for_room: Queued: waiting for room beside the EV chargers that charge

missing.missing_power_sensor: The power sensor is not chosen.
missing.missing_regulation_window: The regulation window is not set.
missing.charger_without_entity: An EV charger without an entity

config.fix_before_saving: Fix the marked settings before saving.
config.not_saved: The configuration was not saved. Fix the marked settings.
config.save_refused_running: The configuration cannot be saved while the regulation runs.
config.leave_text: The changes on the configuration pages are not saved. They are lost if you leave.

locked.title: The configuration is locked
locked.text: The regulation runs. Stop the regulation to change the configuration. When the regulation stops, all regulated appliances and EV chargers are turned off.

warning.appliances_title: Do not turn regulated appliances on or off outside Kraftvakt
warning.chargers_title: Do not turn EV chargers on or off outside Kraftvakt
warning.text: Manual control and automations can disturb the regulation, affect appliances with higher priority and trigger a penalty. Kraftvakt also sets them back when it repeats its commands.

errors.fault_flag_required: Choose a fault flag, or turn the setting off.
errors.duplicate_label: The label must be unique for the appliance.
errors.duplicate_name: The name is already used by another group.
errors.min_current_above_max: The minimum current cannot be above the maximum current.
errors.window_start_equals_end: Start and end cannot be the same.
errors.duplicate_entity: The entity is already used by another appliance or EV charger.
errors.unknown_device: The device no longer exists in Home Assistant.
errors.entity_not_on_device: The entity does not belong to the device of the EV charger, or of the appliance's entity.
errors.invalid_action: Home Assistant cannot read the action.
errors.invalid_template: The template has a syntax error.
errors.default_action_unavailable: The entity has no standard action. Choose a custom action.
errors.unsupported_entity_domain: The entity cannot be used. Choose a number entity.
errors.domain_action_unavailable: The action is not available for the entity. Choose another action.
errors.unsupported_option: The entity does not support this value.
errors.outside_entity_range: Outside the range of the entity.
errors.current_off_unsupported: The entity cannot be set to 0 A, which stops an EV charger turned on and off by the current.
errors.essential_with_variants: An essential appliance cannot have variants. Delete them, or turn the setting off.
errors.essential_with_power_reserve: An essential appliance has no power reserve. Turn the setting off, or turn off Fixed load first.
errors.essential_not_at_top: An essential appliance must be above every other entry in the priority list.
errors.not_a_thermostat: Choose a thermostat, a climate entity.

general.window_measuring: Measuring how often the power sensor reports. It can take up to 30 seconds.
general.window_not_measured: Could not find how often the power sensor reports. Choose it again when it reports regularly.
general.window_too_seldom: The power sensor reports every {interval} s, too seldom for a regulation window of at most {max} s.

power_sensor.label: Power sensor
power_sensor.helper: The total power of the house now, usually from the HAN port of the electricity meter. W or kW.

regulation_window_updates.label: Regulation window
regulation_window_updates.helper: The power sensor reports every {interval} s. Decisions use the average over this many of its updates: more evens out short peaks, fewer reacts faster. {min}–{max} s.

power_sensor_interval_s.label: Update interval of the power sensor

power_limit_w.label: Power limit
power_limit_w.helper: The step in the capacity tariff you want to stay below. The average over the last hour is kept below it. {min}–{max} W, default {default} W.

turn_on_margin_w.label: Turn-on margin
turn_on_margin_w.helper: Appliances are turned on only this far below the power limit, so they are not turned off again at once. {min}–{max} W, default {default} W.

wait_at_limit_s.label: Waiting time at the power limit
wait_at_limit_s.helper: How long an appliance without a fixed load waits before it is turned on when little power is free. The more power is free, the shorter it waits. {min}–{max} s, default {default} s.

penalty_threshold_w.label: Penalty threshold
penalty_threshold_w.helper: How far the average over the last hour may go above the power limit before everything is turned off. {min}–{max} W, default {default} W.

appliance_repeat_increment_factor.label: Increase each time
appliance_repeat_increment_factor.helper: Share of the waiting time at the power limit. Default × {default}.

action_timeout_s.label: Action timeout
action_timeout_s.helper: An action that takes longer is stopped and counts as failed. {min}–{max} s, default {default} s.

power_sensor_timeout_s.label: Power sensor timeout
power_sensor_timeout_s.helper: A power sensor that reports nothing for this long counts as lost, and everything is turned off. A HAN reader usually reports every 10 seconds. {min}–{max} s, default {default} s.

general.penalty_info: A safety valve that should never be needed: if the average over the last hour still goes above the power limit, everything is kept off until the overconsumption is paid back.

advanced.wait_curve_info: How long an appliance without a fixed load waits, by how much power is free. The actual waiting time is rounded up to the next decision.
advanced.repeated_turn_on_info: When the same appliance is turned on again and again with nothing else switched in between, the waiting time grows from the third time. The first two follow the curve; the table shows them at the pivot point.
advanced.command_repeat_info: An appliance or EV charger can change state by itself, for example after a power cut. When it has had no command for this long, it gets the last one again. Excluded ones are left alone.
advanced.timeouts_info: Guards against an action that never finishes and a power sensor that stops reporting.

appliances.priority_sub: Turned on from the top, off from the bottom. Drag to change the order.
appliances.empty: No appliances yet. Add the appliances Kraftvakt may turn off when the consumption is too high.

appliance.variants_info: Give the appliance another place in the priority list at certain times or conditions, for example a higher place for the water heater in the morning. The top variant that applies wins.
appliance.display_values_info: Optional, and not used by the regulation. Shown on the status page for convenience.

entity_id.label: Entity
entity_id.helper: What Kraftvakt turns on and off, for example the switch of a water heater. Its name becomes the name of the appliance.

essential.label: Essential appliance
essential.helper: For an appliance that must always run, such as a freezer. It is kept on, and turned off only during a penalty period. Not for an appliance with variants.

fixed_load.label: Fixed load
fixed_load.helper: Only for an appliance that always draws the same power while it is on, such as a ceiling fan. Never for one with a thermostat or other control of its own: the regulation then works worse.

power_reserve_w.label: Power reserve
power_reserve_w.helper: What the appliance draws while it is on. It is turned on without waiting as soon as this much power is free. Applies to every variant.

variant.condition_info: The variant applies while the expression is true, for example between 05 and 08. Otherwise the appliance keeps its usual place.

action.entity_runs: Runs {service} for the chosen entity with the current as value.
action.no_default: The entity type has no standard action, so the action must be custom.
action.choose_entity: Choose the entity to use the standard action.
action.choose_action_entity: Choose the entity to set the value of.

condition.entity_helper: True only when it is on. Unavailable counts as false.
condition.state_helper: For example a status sensor of the EV charger.
condition.states_helper: Choose or type the states. Every other state counts as the opposite, except unavailable, which counts as false.
condition.template_helper: True only when it gives true. Variables: entity_id, entity.
condition.invalid: The template gives {value}, which is not true or false, so it counts as false.

actively_charging.entity_helper: On while the car charges. Unavailable counts as not charging.
actively_charging.state_helper: For example a status sensor of the EV charger.
actively_charging.states_helper: Choose or type the states. Every other state counts as the opposite, except unavailable, which counts as not charging.
actively_charging.template_helper: True means charging, anything else not charging. Variables: entity_id, entity.
actively_charging.invalid: The template gives {value}, which is not true or false, so it counts as not charging.

charging_power.power_sensor_helper: Above 100 W counts as charging. W or kW.
charging_power.template_helper: The power in W; above 100 W counts as charging. Variables: entity_id, entity.
charging_power.invalid: The template gives {value}, which is not a number, so it counts as not charging.

display_power.power_sensor_helper: A sensor of the same device as the entity. W or kW.
display_power.template_helper: The power in W, also from another device. Variables: entity_id, entity.
display_power.invalid: The template gives {value}, which is not a number, so nothing is shown.

display_temperature.temperature_sensor_helper: A temperature sensor of the same device as the entity, or a thermostat's current or set temperature.
display_temperature.template_helper: A temperature in the unit of Home Assistant, also from another device. Variables: entity_id, entity.
display_temperature.invalid: The template gives {value}, which is not a number, so nothing is shown.

fault.entity_helper: On means a fault. Unavailable is no fault.
fault.state_helper: For example a status sensor of the EV charger.
fault.states_helper: Choose or type the states. Every other state counts as the opposite, except unavailable, which is no fault.
fault.template_helper: True means a fault, anything else no fault. Variables: entity_id, entity.
fault.invalid: The template gives {value}, which is not true or false, so it counts as no fault.

charging.name: Name
charging.name_sub: Shown in the priority list and on the status page.
charging.one_at_a_time: One EV charger at a time
charging.one_at_a_time_sub: Only one car in the group charges at a time. While none charges, every car may wait at the minimum current, and the first that draws power gets the turn.
charging.dynamic_order_sub:
Off: the charging priority below always applies, so a car higher up that draws power takes over from one charging below it.
On: EV chargers that charge go first, and the others wait their turn.
charging.chargers_sub: Highest at the top. Drag an EV charger to another group to move it.
charging.no_groups: No groups of EV chargers yet. Add a group, and then its EV chargers.
charging.delete_group_not_empty: Move or delete its EV chargers to delete the group.
charging.switches_info: Each EV charger gets three switches you can use while the regulation runs: «‹charger› excluded from regulation», «‹charger› override charging window» and «‹charger› finish charging after charging window».
charging.finishes_after_window: finishes ongoing charging after the window
charging.switched_by_current: turned on and off by the current

charger.profile_applied: Filled in from the charger profile {profile}. Check every field before you save.

override_ends.charging_stopped: When the car no longer charges

device_id.label: Device
device_id.helper: The EV charger in Home Assistant. Its entities are chosen below, and filled in when Kraftvakt knows the charger.

entity_id.label: Charger entity
entity_id.helper: Usually the switch that allows charging.

min_current_power_w.label: Power at minimum current
min_current_power_w.helper: What the car draws at the minimum current, about 1400 W on one phase. The car starts charging only when this much power is free. {min}–{max} W, default {default} W, 6 A on three phases.

car_connected.label: Car connected
car_connected.helper: An EV charger without a car is not activated. Unavailable counts as not connected.

actively_charging.label: Actively charging
actively_charging.helper: The charging power is required, and tells how much the car draws. The charging on/off is optional, and may tell sooner that the car charges.

cloud_controlled.label: Cloud-controlled EV charger
cloud_controlled.helper: For an EV charger controlled over the internet. It gets fewer repeated commands, and its power is kept free while the car starts charging.

start_delay_s.label: Start delay
start_delay_s.helper: How long the car may take to start charging after the EV charger is activated. Its power at minimum current is kept free meanwhile. {min}–{max} s, default {default} s.

deactivate_on_fault.label: Deactivate on fault
deactivate_on_fault.helper: While a fault flag shows a fault, the EV charger is stopped and the others in the group may charge. Unavailable is no fault.

charging_window.label: Charging window
charging_window.helper: The EV charger charges only within this time each day, for example at night. Off: it may always charge.

finish_after_window.label: Finish charging after the charging window
finish_after_window.helper: A car that is charging when the charging window ends may go on until it stops. It then waits for the next charging window.

override_ends.label: End the override
override_ends.helper: When the switch «‹charger› override charging window» turns itself off. It can be turned on before the car arrives.

switched_by_current.label: Charging is turned on and off by
switched_by_current.helper: Choose the current for an EV charger that has no way to turn charging on and off: 0 A stops it.

charger.charging_current_info: The current is raised and lowered one ampere at a time by the free power. The minimum is the lowest current the car charges with, usually 6 A, and the maximum what the EV charger and its fuse allow.
